name: Baseline: central assumptions
description: v0.2 defaults from docs/model-spec.md section 10. All levers at central values, structural ensemble on, no shocks.

name: Configuration: U.S. closed (no regional layer)
description: The baseline run for the United States alone: no shared production ramp, no trade feedback, no rents from or to other regions. Used with the regional decomposition to show how much of the U.S. headline comes from the ten-region configuration.

name: EU AI Act delayed 2y + DeepSeek open frontier 2027
description: Example what-if from the brief. Diff vs baseline: regulation.EU.ai_act, one shock.

name: Policy: retraining subsidy 50% of wage
description: Retraining subsidy at 50% of the wage for enrolled workers, deficit-financed (spec §6.5, minimal wiring §A.16).

name: Policy: $500/month basic income, tax-financed
description: A $500 monthly payment to every adult, financed by an income-tax surcharge that covers the payment in full, with a 30% tax on AI spend covering part of the bill on top. Balanced-budget by construction: the surcharge takes back what the transfer pays out, so the run shows the redistribution, not a deficit stimulus (the deficit-financed version is variant policy-ubi-deficit).

name: Variant: $500/month basic income, deficit-financed
description: The same $500 monthly payment to every adult with the 30% AI tax covering a small part and the deficit the rest. About $1.7 trillion a year of deficit spending is outside the model's fiscal range (it has no inflation, interest-rate or debt response), so its employment effect is overstated; the run is kept only to show the validity flag (meta.validity.fiscal_warning). Read the tax-financed run (policy-ubi-ai-tax) for the policy's effect.

name: Policy: wage insurance 50% for 2 years
description: Half of the earnings loss of re-employed displaced workers replaced for two years, financed by an AI tax.

name: Policy: 36-hour standard week
description: Standard week shortened to 36 hours; FTE spread over more heads at proportionally lower pay per head (P.72 conversion).

name: Preset: Acemoglu 2024
description: Report-replication preset (spec §8.4). Only directly exposed (E1) tasks within the decade, no reinstatement, no demand feedback, low intensity; targets TFP no more than +0.66% and GDP about +1% over ten years. The v0.3 application layer (embodied automation, output substitution, traded services) is switched off: the study modelled generative AI on tasks only.

name: Preset: Goldman Sachs 2023
description: Report-replication preset (spec §8.4). Default feasibility, near-unit-elastic output demand with high pass-through of cost savings to prices, historical reinstatement, slightly higher intensity; reproduces GDP about +7% over ten years with employment roughly flat, which is the report's narrative. The v0.3 application layer (embodied automation, output substitution, traded services) is switched off: the study modelled generative AI on tasks only.

name: Preset: IMF 2024
description: Report-replication preset (spec §8.4). Exposure with a complementarity split: about 60% of advanced-economy employment exposed, half of it complementary (augmentation-leaning). Targets the IMF's qualitative result: wide exposure, roughly half augmented, rising inequality. The v0.3 application layer (embodied automation, output substitution, traded services) is switched off: the study modelled generative AI on tasks only.

name: Preset: Seba / RethinkX 2026 (humanoids and TaaS)
description: RethinkX's 2024–2026 labour claims and the 2026 'Rethinking Energy, Mobility, and Materials' roadmap as levers: humanoid labour under $10/hour at entry and under $1/hour before 2035, robots doing as much work as people by the late 2030s, TaaS carrying 80% of urban passenger miles by 2035. Pushes the manipulation class as hard as the transport preset pushes driving: the fastest clocks, the top of the ever-automatable range, maximum utilization, the lowest unit price, accelerated approval everywhere, and induced demand at twice the catalogue. The forecast scoreboard tests these claims against the model.

name: Preset: Seba / RethinkX disruption
description: Tony Seba's technology-disruption framework as scenario levers: cost curves at electronics-like learning rates, fleets built at the fastest historical ramps, high utilization (transport as a service), approvals accelerated where fleets already operate, embodiment clocks coupled tightly to the software frontier, and an eroding preference for human-made content. Reproduces the shape of his S-curve claims; the forecast scoreboard compares his 2017 and 2020 numbers with the model's.

name: Variant: employers cut through layoffs
description: The same AI, with employers that cut ahead of attrition twice as readily as the fitted baseline: half of each quarter's required headcount reduction is taken as layoffs at once (lever labor.layoff_first_share 0.5 against the baseline's 0.25, which is fitted to the AI-cited job cuts employers announced in 2025 and the first half of 2026), net occupational attrition at the bottom of its range (P.63) and the layoff pace at the top (P.64). The same total jobs, borne by incumbents rather than entrants.

name: Variant: market-clearing wages
description: The same AI, with wages that absorb excess supply at the top of the elasticity range: wage adjustment toward the wage-curve target at the top of its range (P.73 = 0.6 per quarter), productivity pass-through to wages at the top of its range (P.74 = 0.6), reinstatement of displaced work in new tasks at the top of its range (P.61 = 0.8) and the output demand response to lower costs at the top of the P.60 range (scale 1.5). Read beside the baseline for the wage effect and the under-25 share of jobs lost (review §2.7).
